measured_on: Core Ultra 9 285H, Arc 140T (DX12), Windows 11 26340, while other lanes were compiling on the same machine. Every picture was rendered headless with `proteus shot --world` from a journal of a real session; no window was opened at any point.

done.what: Ctrl+Shift+W shows the session's work as one scene: the process tree, a timeline of every process, the output printed per slice of time, and counters (running, spawned, failed, elapsed, session). Esc or Ctrl+Shift+W returns. The session keeps running underneath; no resize is sent to the program
done.evidence: forge/out/world-build.png, world-many-mid-build.png, world-5000.png (rendered from real journals); the window path itself is compiled and unit-tested but has never been run, see known_issues

done.what: A left-to-right tree from the shell, each node at the row of its first child, orthogonal connectors, columns as wide as their widest label. A node says its image name, its arguments with long paths cut to their last two parts, its exit code if it failed, and its life if that was a second or more. Running: accent, filled mark. Exit 0: dim green, hollow mark. Non-zero: red, with the code in text. The path from the shell to a failure is drawn in red

When the tree has more rows than the window, detail falls in a fixed order until it fits: finished successes are counted into groups by name first (`rustc x26  exit 0`), failures next, running processes last. Of each kind the most recent stay expanded, as many as fit. A failure is never counted among successes: failures that cannot all be drawn become a red counted group (`cmd x24  24 failed`), and the most recent failure always keeps its own node. If even that does not fit, the rows left out are stated on screen with their counts
done.evidence: world tests finished_identical_siblings_are_counted_and_failures_and_running_stay_expanded, failures_that_cannot_all_be_drawn_are_counted_in_red_never_hidden_among_successes; forge/out/world-5000.png (4,999 real processes in 22 rows), world-5000-1200x700-2x.png (the same in 6 rows)

done.what: One span per process from its start to its end on a shared axis, coloured by exit state, one band per depth with as many rows as ran side by side (up to 6). The axis ends at the latest event, not at the wall clock: a running process's span ends at the right edge. Beneath it, bytes printed per slice of time, linear, each bar drawn over exactly the stretch of time it counts; the slice length and the tallest bar are stated
done.evidence: world tests time_ends_at_the_latest_event_and_nothing_reads_a_clock, output_is_counted_into_exact_slices_and_no_byte_is_lost; forge/out/world-many-mid-build.png (three compilers at a time, as CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=3 made them)

done.what: A process starting lights its node (its label unfolds like arriving text and its box casts the accent into the light field); a process failing casts red. History replayed to a window is placed without being lit. Nothing else moves
done.evidence: forge/out/world-many-mid-build.png (60 ms after a compiler started), world-build-as-it-fails.png (90 ms after the build failed); world test nothing_asks_for_a_frame_unless_the_picture_changed

done.what: The mouse over a node, a group or a span shows a card: the whole command line (wrapped, as many rows as the window holds), exit code, life, pid, start, CPU time; for a group, its counts and its most recent members. The same process is outlined in the tree and on the timeline. A frame is drawn only when the mouse moves onto something else
done.evidence: forge/out/world-build-hover-node.png, world-build-hover-span.png, world-build-hover-1200x700.png, world-loop30-hover-group.png; world test everything_can_be_hovered_at_every_size (every node, group and span of three sessions at five sizes)

done.what: The wheel zooms the timeline about the mouse; Left/Right slide it, Up/Down or +/- zoom, 0 or Home shows the whole session, End jumps to the latest moment. A zoomed axis says what stretch it shows. A zoomed range that includes the latest moment follows it

`proteus shot --world --journal FILE [--until SECS] [--reveal-ms N] [--hover X,Y] [--zoom FROM,TO] [--time N]` renders the view from a journal through the same scene builder and GPU path as the window. `--world --cmd "EXE ARGS" [--cwd DIR]` runs a real session now, journaled, feeding the view event by event as a window is fed, and says where the journal is. It prints what was drawn in numbers, how long frames are owed after the latest event, and the scene build time

A window that attaches to a running session is replayed its output with no times. The view does not draw that as a burst at the moment of attaching: when it is first opened it reads the record times from the session's journal (the daemon now tells the window where the journal is) and places exactly the replayed bytes by them. Without a readable journal those bytes stay off the timeline and the view says how many

known_issues: The window path has never run. The toggle, the keys, the wheel, hover, the per-frame hook and the journal read on first opening are compiled, and everything they call is unit-tested (world.rs Live; renderer/scene.rs on the real GPU), but no window could be opened here. The first person to press Ctrl+Shift+W is the first test of app.rs's wiring.

Idle CPU of a window was not re-measured after the frame loop changed. It gained: one atomic read and a comparison on every wake (output is placed on the timeline whether or not the view is up), and, only while the view is up, a scene build after each grid build.

Failures do not always stay expanded. When there are more failures than rows the older ones are counted in a red group; the brief said failures stay expanded. The most recent always does, and no failure is ever counted among successes.
While the view is up every key is the view's, including Ctrl+Shift+D (detach), copy and paste, and font size. Clicks, the wheel and typed text (IME) do not reach the program either.

Output is placed at the moment the window woke for it. A window that is not being drawn (minimised) wakes once and then places everything that arrived meanwhile at its next frame. Live output is also counted in 20 ms slices, so at the deepest zoom a bar and the process that printed it can be up to 20 ms apart.

Opening the view for the first time in a window that reattached reads the session's journal on the window's own thread: 18 to 23 ms for a 1.9 MB journal measured here; a journal of hundreds of megabytes would stall the window for that long, once.

A daemon built before this lane does not say where the journal is: output from before the window attached is then left off the timeline, and the view says how many bytes. A journal with no process records has a clock known only to the second, and is treated the same way.

Scene build time grows with the number of processes held: about 1.4 ms at 5,000 (generated), so about 6 ms would be expected at the window's cap of 20,000. Not measured at 20,000. Nothing is cached between builds: a hover rebuilds everything.
A long-lived window holds the most recent 20,000 ended processes (procs lane). Older ones are counted in 'spawned' but no longer drawn; the view says how many.

The timeline shows at most 8 depth bands and 6 rows per band; deeper processes share the last band and more than 6 at once share rows, overlapping. Spans that fall on the same pixels in the same colour are drawn once.
Columns share the width equally when every column wants more than its share, so a column of long compiler command lines is cut at the same width as a column holding one short node.
A non-zero exit is drawn as a failure whatever the program means by it (findstr exits 1 when it finds nothing; so does the sample).

Light from several starts in one group adds up at that group's node; in the 1200x700 capture of the 40-crate build the glow around `rustc x34` is strong. Levels were chosen from stills and have not been judged in motion by a person.
The card can cover the node it describes when it fits neither under nor over it (a long command line in a small window).

(review) Fixed, each with a test on a recorded session that failed first: a failure folded into the last column's node could lose its tag, so the header counted '1 failed' over a tree of nothing but clean exits (seen at 2360x1520 on a chain eight deep, and at 1200x700 on one five deep); the hover card could be wider than a narrow window (its facts line was never wrapped); the one-line header dropped how the session ended, and at 700 px ran its last counter off the edge; placing a reattached session's history cost the product of its length and how long the window had been attached (774 ms for 60,000 slices under 60,000, GENERATED; now 1.7 ms); a held Ctrl+Shift+W flipped the view for as long as it was held, and a held Esc, having closed the view, was typed into the program underneath (the key logic is tested in world.rs; the four lines in app.rs that call it are, like the rest of the window wiring, unrun).

(review) A node is named by its image, as the OS reports it, with the arguments from its command line. They can disagree: `cargo build` run through rustup's launcher is drawn as `rustup build --offline` (the image really is rustup.exe; the card shows the command line as typed).

(review) Characters wider than a cell (CJK, emoji) are drawn squeezed into one cell each, and combining marks take a cell of their own: legible, nothing overlaps, but not shaped. Seen in forge/out, on a session with such command lines.

(review) A path cut to its end and then cut again by its column shows two ellipses in a row (`link /NOLOGO ......`). A counter that does not fit the header whole is left out rather than cut (elapsed goes first); under about 700 px at a 30 px font that happens.

(review) On the timeline a mark is never narrower than 2 logical pixels and failures are drawn last, so in a long session red takes more of the band than failures take of the processes (200 failures in 5,001 processes over 86 s: about a third of the band's width).
